segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Madam Lim, come in, sit down. How have you been since July?

segments.speaker: elder
segments.text: Doctor ah, so-so lah. The knee still pain when I go down the stairs.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Let me look at your blood test first. Your HbA1c has come up to 8.2, which is higher than last time.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: So I am going to titrate the metformin up to 850 milligrams twice a day.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: The X-ray of your knee shows osteoarthritis in the medial compartment. It is wear and tear on the inner side of the joint.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: I do not want to give you an NSAID because of your kidneys, so I will refer you to physiotherapy instead.

segments.speaker: elder
segments.text: The new tablet, the one for sleeping, make me a bit blur in the morning.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: That is the amitriptyline. I started you on 25 milligrams. Let us bring it down to 10 milligrams and see if the drowsiness settles.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: You are still taking the amlodipine for your blood pressure, correct?

segments.speaker: elder
segments.text: The white one, morning time. Yes.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Your weight is down 2 kilos since July. Are you finishing your meals?

segments.speaker: elder
segments.text: Sometimes half only. Not so hungry.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Then I want someone keeping an eye on that. If you are still leaving half your meals in two weeks, we need to look at it properly.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Come back in 6 weeks. If the knee gets worse, or you feel giddy when you stand up, come earlier.
